fields.question: Why distinguish source and destination tokens in RouteOPD?
fields.answer: Student-overestimated items have excess mass, underestimated items need mass. Explicit transport identifies where corrections come from and go instead of indiscriminate matching.
fields.example: Move mass from overpreferred wording to a teacher-supported key digit.

fields.question: How does transporting mass differ from replacing the student distribution with teacher probabilities?
fields.answer: Transport addresses selected discrepancies, not every coordinate. Require nonnegativity, conservation and defined source/destination; ordinary softmax isn't routing.
fields.example: Unrouted candidates can remain unchanged, unlike full replacement.

fields.question: What invariants should RouteOPD transport check?
fields.answer: Never remove more mass than available; additions equal removals; final probabilities nonnegative and normalized. No transport at zero gap. A kernel doesn't reproduce teacher-model training.
fields.example: Removing one unit and adding only half breaks normalization.

fields.question: Why isn't transport equivalent to boosting every high-probability teacher token?
fields.answer: Select sources/destinations by student over/underestimation relative to teacher, not absolute teacher mass. This traces corrections and conserves probability. Interpretability doesn't prove teacher correctness; control support and evaluation.
fields.example: An already popular word in both models may need no boost; a teacher-supported overlooked word can receive mass.

fields.question: Why use a verifier to correct OPDVR teacher reward signs?
fields.answer: Teacher/student log ratios can oppose trajectory correctness. Retain only sign-consistent credit to avoid reinforcing errors or suppressing correct trajectories.
fields.example: Do not punish a different correct solution just because the teacher dislikes it.

fields.question: How does OPDVR differ from adding another RL loss?
fields.answer: It removes the inconsistent part of implicit reward rather than mixing two losses with compensating weights. The objectives differ.
fields.example: Zero out positive teacher reward on an error rather than add a negative term hoping it cancels.

fields.question: Which half-axis does OPDVR retain for correct and wrong trajectories?
fields.answer: Correct keeps nonnegative log ratios; wrong keeps nonpositive; zero stays zero. Verifier is a fixed training signal, not rollout input. Local candidates aren't Qwen math rollouts.
fields.example: A positive log ratio on a failure becomes zero, not a sign-flipped extra penalty.

fields.question: Why retain only nonnegative teacher signal for success and nonpositive for failure?
fields.answer: Token ratios can conflict with terminal outcome. One-sided ReLU uses verifiable correctness to gate implicit reward, not add a standalone RL loss. Coarse labels don't prove each token and remain scoring-only.
fields.example: Suppress a negative imitation signal for a correct alternative without requiring teacher wording.

fields.question: Should OPDSearch+ students imitate search-result text as their own output?
fields.answer: No. Students generate queries, reasoning and answers; search observations condition later actions. Teacher guidance doesn't make tool output a student target.
fields.example: Use a webpage excerpt to ask the next query rather than role-play the returned page verbatim.

fields.question: How does on-student search distillation differ from offline teacher demonstrations?
fields.answer: The teacher sees states and prefixes the student actually reached, including mistakes; offline continuations come from teacher states. Different recovery coverage isn't a universal performance ranking.
fields.example: Online scoring sees a wrong first query that a correct teacher demonstration never visits.

fields.question: Does local OPDSearch+ execute real query, reasoning and answer tokens?
fields.answer: No. Candidate-level process axes proxy generation/search feedback without real index/model. The real mask covers only generated text, never returned documents.
fields.example: A process score doesn't mean a Wikipedia search ran.

fields.question: Why distill from a frozen general teacher before continuing agent RL?
fields.answer: Dense guidance on student search traces improves the starting behavior. Verifiable RL then adapts to environmental results rather than remain bound to teacher preferences. No specialized teacher training required; bias and proxy limits remain.
fields.example: Learn to ask workable queries, then let retrieved evidence and final verification adjust habits.

fields.question: Why estimate reasoning progress independently in R²-OPD?
fields.answer: Teacher preference needn't help solve the task. Compare independent progress and mask conflicting supervision rather than equate style with reasoning.
fields.example: A fluent explanation may score high with teacher while moving farther from the solution.

fields.question: How does rank filtering differ from summing rewards?
fields.answer: Filtering requires agreement to retain teacher signal. Addition lets a large score offset a poor one. Agreement doesn't prove either judge correct.
fields.example: A huge teacher score cannot buy back a span rejected by progress disagreement.

fields.question: What identities must both R²-OPD rankings share?
fields.answer: Score the same spans of the same trajectories and align by identity; define ties. Local candidates do not run a real progress judge.
fields.example: Match a span across rankings, not the third list position.

fields.question: Why mask conflicting teacher and progress rankings instead of trusting teacher?
fields.answer: Style can receive teacher approval without useful progress. Independent ordering checks direction. Masking signals uncertainty, not proof a span is wrong, and the progress evaluator still needs validation.
fields.example: Don't reinforce a polished long explanation if it leaves the key constraint unsolved.

fields.question: Why keep a reference alongside SR-OPSD self-teacher?
fields.answer: Self-teacher can drift or become overly strong. Reference anchors the geometrically interpolated target and Rényi sensitivity control instead of trusting self-teacher alone.
fields.example: Retain some prior support when teacher strongly favors a new mode.

fields.question: How does geometric interpolation differ from arithmetic averaging?
fields.answer: Combine weighted log probabilities then normalize; arithmetic directly mixes mass. Low support from one side affects them differently, and formulas are not interchangeable.
fields.example: A nearly zero mass on one side can depress a geometric target more than arithmetic average.

fields.question: Why form SR-OPSD targets in log space and normalize explicitly?
fields.answer: Power products underflow. Weighted log-space softmax yields a stable distribution on aligned teacher/reference vocabulary. No full model/Rényi experiments locally.
fields.example: Raw elementwise product without normalization isn't a probability distribution.

fields.question: Why geometrically mix self-teacher and reference?
fields.answer: Log-space combination treats tails and disagreement differently from arithmetic mixtures. Reference anchors, teacher guides and divergence regulates projection sensitivity. Equal endpoints do not make two interpolation methods equivalent.
fields.example: Distributions favoring different tokens can give very different intermediate geometric and arithmetic targets.

fields.question: Why is U-OPSD privileged view still externally unsupervised?
fields.answer: It comes from internal sampling consensus, without external answers/reward or a larger teacher. One view sees an extra internally produced signal, not independently verified truth.
fields.example: A short self-selected consensus solution can still be a shared error.

fields.question: Why distinguish shortest consensus answer from arbitrary shortest answer?
fields.answer: First require majority agreement, then minimize length within eligible outputs. The shortest unrestricted may be an empty or outlier answer. Consensus isn't gold.
fields.example: A short erroneous refusal doesn't become privileged guidance because it saves tokens.

fields.question: Can U-OPSD use gold before choosing an internal reference?
fields.answer: No. Use predictions only for consensus, thresholds and length. Gold is for independent evaluation. Deterministic mini-suite isn't full multi-turn self-distillation.
fields.example: Filtering correctness before voting smuggles answer information into training.

fields.question: How avoid treating shortest consensus as truth without gold?
fields.answer: Consensus selects a reference and repair targets as pseudo-supervision, not correctness verification. Shared errors may be reinforced. Report internal agreement separately from external holdout and keep gold out of student inputs.
fields.example: Several responses can use the same wrong formula; the shortest still isn't a standard solution.
